name: Pulling coconut oil for gums

lead: Oil pulling means swishing an edible oil such as coconut oil in the mouth and spitting it out. It comes from Ayurvedic tradition and is used for gum health, fresher breath and a cleaner-feeling mouth.

Practitioners say it improves oral health and that the oil pulls out toxins; Wikipedia reports no credible evidence for a toxin-removal mechanism, and some commentators attribute any effect to the mechanical swishing. The American Dental Association has said no reliable studies support it, while the Canadian Dental Association said in 2014 it was not convinced of benefits but did not think it would cause harm.

paras: People swish a spoonful of oil for several minutes, usually in the morning, and spit it out like a mouthwash before brushing. Coconut is the most common choice, and sunflower, sesame, olive and herbal oils are also used.
The Canadian Dental Association did not expect harm, and the sources consulted do not discuss specific adverse events. It is used alongside, not instead of, brushing and flossing.

angle.text: Oil pulling comes from Ayurvedic practice and is used for gum health and a cleaner, fresher-feeling mouth. The ADA reports no reliable studies supporting it, and the Canadian Dental Association does not expect harm.

lead: Oil pulling with coconut oil is the practice of swishing the oil in the mouth for a period and then spitting it out, like a mouthwash, in the hope of improving gum and oral health. It comes from Ayurvedic medicine, and sunflower, sesame, olive and herbal oils are also used.[1]

Practitioners say it improves oral health, and promoters often say it pulls out toxins. The Wikipedia summary reports no credible evidence for a toxin-removal mechanism.[1] The American Dental Association has said there are no reliable scientific studies supporting oil pulling for oral hygiene benefits, while the Canadian Dental Association (2014) said it did not think the practice would cause harm but was not convinced of particular benefits.[1]

paras: The user holds a small amount of edible oil in the mouth, moves it around, and spits it out afterwards.[1]

A 2016 systematic review of randomised trials on oral hygiene (Gbinigie and colleagues) urged caution because the included studies were few, underpowered and small.[1] Commentators including Steven Novella (2014) have suggested any benefit may come from mechanical swishing, and a 2013 paper (Lakshmi and colleagues) noted that no mechanism has been identified.[1]

Small randomised trials have been reviewed; the 2016 systematic review by Gbinigie and colleagues urged caution because of small, underpowered studies.[1] The sources consulted do not give specific gum-disease trial results.

lore.intro: Oil pulling is discussed as a natural alternative to mouthwash for gums and breath.

claims.claim: Swishing coconut oil heals gums and pulls out toxins
